correctness.rationale: Finite colored bisimulation refinement corresponds to atoms of the Boolean modal algebra generated by one marked set P. Duplicate row/column profiles yield valuation-preserving automorphisms. A non-Ferrers 2x2 checkerboard can be saturated to mixed core rows/columns; classes labeled (core-row marker, core-column marker, P bit) form a nontrivial color-preserving bisimulation, preventing singleton definability. Conversely Ferrers nested profiles with every row/column distinct admit recursive definition and removal of unique monochromatic rows/columns by row/column diamonds, preserving distinguishability; intersections define every singleton. Sorted Ferrers row lengths must contain 1..n−1 and optional 0,n, leaving exactly two balanced or one adjacent-side staircases. Each has trivial row/column-label stabilizer; counts 2(k!)^2, m!n! and 0 as stated, including the 1x1 boundary. Independent modal successor-set refinement on ALL 74,954 binary matrices of m,n in 1..4 confirmed the theorem, not substituted for infinite proof.
